title: Accounting Basics: Key Terms
description: Essential accounting vocabulary, from the accounting equation and debits and credits to the three main financial statements.
subject: business-economics

cards.definition: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Every transaction keeps both sides in balance.
Every transaction is recorded in at least two accounts, with total debits always equal to total credits.
Records revenue when it is earned and expenses when they are incurred, regardless of when cash changes hands.
Records revenue and expenses only when cash is actually received or paid.
A resource the business controls that is expected to provide future benefit, such as cash, inventory, or equipment.
An obligation the business owes to others, such as a loan or an unpaid supplier bill.
The owners' residual claim on the business: what is left of the assets after liabilities are subtracted.
Income earned from a business's normal operations, such as selling goods or providing services.
A cost incurred to earn revenue during a period, such as rent, wages, or utilities.
An entry on the left side of an account. It increases assets and expenses, and decreases liabilities, equity, and revenue.
An entry on the right side of an account. It increases liabilities, equity, and revenue, and decreases assets and expenses.
Shows a company's assets, liabilities, and equity at a single point in time.
Reports revenue, expenses, and the resulting net income or loss over a period of time.
Shows cash moving in and out over a period, grouped into operating, investing, and financing activities.
Money customers owe the business for goods or services already delivered on credit.
Money the business owes suppliers for goods or services it bought on credit.
The direct costs of making or buying the goods a business sold during the period.
Revenue minus cost of goods sold.
Revenue minus all expenses for the period. When the result is negative, it is a net loss.
The cumulative net income a company has kept in the business rather than paid out as dividends.
Spreading the cost of a long-lived physical asset, like a machine, over its useful life as an expense.
Current assets minus current liabilities. A measure of a company's ability to cover its short-term obligations.
The master record of all of a business's accounts and the transactions posted to them.
A list of every ledger account's balance, used to check that total debits equal total credits.
